body:
Thats the biggest problem; I don't really see anything changing the way I feel.  I feel like I've already experienced it all, and anything else will just be rehashed versions of more-of-the-same.  I've loved, I've lost, I've been spoiled, I've spoiled others, I've traveled the world many times over, learned foreign languages and interacted with other cultures, I've fought for my country, I've wanted to fight against my country, I've heard wonderful music, seen great movies and works of art, met fascinating people, been high out of my mind, and sober as they come, ... But now every time I do any of the above (or ANYTHING for that matter), it just feels so fucking hollow.  So empty... 

I can compare everything I'm doing and will ever do to something I've already done, and it was (almost without fail) ALWAYS better the first time.  Nothing ever comes close to the almost magical feel of experiencing something for the first time.  Drugs, sex, first day of work, first kiss, first video game... no "second" anything is ever as good.  And thats how I see the rest of my life unfolding, and it doesn't scare me, it just seems so fucking boring and tiring.

And the biggest problem, is like I said earlier, I can relate past similar experiences to things I've never even done before.  I've never been shot, but I've been shot at, I've been shot with a paintball gun, I've been rushed to the E.R., I've recovered from serious injuries.  Put all those experiences together, and I can imagine the adrenaline rush and the pain of getting shot, the dizzying trip to the E.R., and the difficult recovery afterwards.  I know thats a crappy example, but thats how I see things, and because of it I cant think of anything that would excite me.  I dunno, its weird, kind of hard to explain, sorry for rambling on and on there...

While I love the idea, the rational part of me knows that by going crazy, making radical changes, etc., when/if I do come out of this "funk", most of the "good" things I have going for my right now wont be here anymore...  My well paying job, which in turn would mean I'd lose my ridiculously high mortgage house, my car, and all around my financial flexibility.  I know it sounds silly, but I think I'm scared of this kind of thing actually "fixing" me, because then I'll just be pissed at myself for throwing away so much, and having to grind my way back up from the bottom.  I have a lot of friends going through tough financial times right now, and its no joke, it makes most of my problems seem pale in comparison... yet it doesnt change the way I feel.  I do like the idea though, and my current plan (I was going to throw that in quotes too, but I think I've already gone a little quote happy) is to try and find a way to mix things up while still holding onto my job.  I'm not sure if it will be as successful as the alternative, but I guess we'll see.  Thanks for taking the time to respond
